pdp.description: A faithful take on an archive piece from the maison, preserving its original structure. Knitted in English rib with shaped decreases along the raglan, it has a mock-neck collar and a full-length front closure with an exposed metal zip. The polished silver-tone hardware includes exposed teeth and an elongated rectangular pull. The vertical rib knit falls straight over the torso, then gathers slightly at the waist through the ribbed hem. Raglan sleeves give natural comfort across the shoulders. Pocketless and unlined, the cardigan is hip length and works both on its own and under a coat.

3051924538.headline: Iterate: forecast sell-through is 56.8% against a 65% target, and the constraint is conversion (0.83%), not interest.
3051924538.summary: The 80% interval (51.6%–62.0%) doesn't reach 65%, so the statistical decision is iterate and the comments give no reason to change it. The interest is there: save rate 3.14% and 79 waitlist sign-ups. But only 14 people pre-ordered (conversion 0.83%, 17th percentile). The comments partly explain why: 14 of 60 ask about size, 8 mention the zip and 5 ask which wool it is and whether it itches. These are doubts that a design change (two-way zip) and information in all content can resolve. Don't order now. If ordering after the second test, the cap is 220 units, not the usual 650.

insights.title: The bottleneck is conversion, not visibility
insights.evidence: Save rate 3.14% (33rd percentile), conversion 0.83% (17th percentile), pre-orders per €1k 5.6 (8th percentile). In the archive, launches with conversion ≥1.45% have ST between 52% and 79%; the Black Mini Cabas (1.45%) is the lowest, with a 1.21% save rate.

insights.title: Interest doesn't turn into purchase
insights.evidence: 79 waitlist sign-ups vs 14 pre-orders, i.e. 5.6 sign-ups per pre-order. The 1692 sessions produced a 0.83% conversion.

insights.title: The 18-24 budget returns little
insights.evidence: 18-24: €450, 1 pre-order, conversion 0.29%, even though the CTR is the highest (0.69%). 25-44: €1650, 11 of 14 pre-orders, i.e. 6.7 per €1k vs 2.2 per €1k for 18-24.

insights.title: Differences between content and markets are too small to decide on
insights.evidence: Each piece of content has 0–3 pre-orders. Back view, over-the-shoulder glance has 3 (conv. 1.66%), Direct flash and Sculpted grey 0, but with about 170–200 sessions zero is compatible with chance. Markets have 3–4 pre-orders each (Italy 0.60%, UK 1.07%) on equal spend (€625). The clearest signal is that the formats where fit is judged get fewer saves: packshot 2.20%, on-model 2.38%, against an average of 3.14%.

insights.title: No performance decline over the 10 days, but sessions are falling
insights.evidence: 6 pre-orders on days 1-5 and 8 on days 6-10, with 3 zero days (d3, d5, d8). Sessions go from 203 and 208 (d1, d2) to 161 (d10) on the same €250 daily spend.

3051924538|a_mvca3108uyr9,a_mvc9y3chm63k.headline: Iterate: forecast sell-through is 57.6% against a 65% target, the look is liked, but conversion (0.75%) is held back by open questions on wool, zip and size.
3051924538|a_mvca3108uyr9,a_mvc9y3chm63k.summary: The statistical decision is ITERATE and the comments support it. Save rate is 3.12% (percentile 50), but conversion is 0.75% (percentile 17) and pre-orders per €1k are 5.6 (percentile 0). Beige and the rib-knit mock neck are praised (26 of 60 comments), while 22 of 60 comments are questions on wool, zip, size and care that block the purchase. The 80% interval (40.8%–74.3%) contains the target, so this is not a stop. The base is thin: 14 pre-orders and a regression on 6 launches.

insights.title: Forecast is below target but the target is inside the interval
insights.evidence: Sell-through 57.6% (80%: 40.8%–74.3%) vs 65% target. Regression on 6 launches, R² 0.89, with only 14 pre-orders behind it.

insights.title: Conversion is the gap, not interest
insights.evidence: Save rate 3.12% is percentile 50, conversion 0.75% is percentile 17. With save rate unchanged, conversion of about 1.17% would give 65% (each +0.1pp adds about 1.75 points of ST). The closest past launch, Tobacco Mohair Zip Cardigan, had 1.05% and 64% ST.

insights.title: Comments show what blocks the purchase
insights.evidence: Of 60 comments: 22 are questions on wool/itch (5), zip (6), size (9) and care (2). 6 more say the price is fair only 'if it's proper wool'. Colour and knit are positive in 26 of 60 (13 + 13).

insights.title: UGC, the UK and 35-44 convert best; Italy converts worst
insights.evidence: UGC reel: 1.72% conv, 4 pre-orders on €303. UK: 1.48% (6 pre-orders, 9.6 per €1k). Italy: 0.18% (1 pre-order, 1.6 per €1k) despite the most sessions (547). 35-44: 1.00% vs 0.54% for 18-24.

insights.title: Pre-orders came early and traffic faded
insights.evidence: Days 1-5: 10 pre-orders, about 214 sessions a day. Days 6-10: 4 pre-orders, about 161 sessions a day. Day 8 had 0.

Smooth semi-rigid cognac leather, not pebbled. Instead of the single strap, two short, wide, simple handles, one on the front and one on the back, attached at the top edge. Internal magnetic closure at the centre of the rim. A central vertical seam on the front, from the top edge to the base. Flat base with slightly rounded corners. No lettering and no logo. Measurements: W 28 cm, H 22 cm, D 10 cm (body, handles excluded).
